# Node.js Engineering Rules

## Layered Architecture & Portability
- Keep business logic independent of web frameworks (Express, Fastify, NestJS).
- Framework-specific code must exist only in the entry/transport layer.
- Enforce strict flow: Transport (Routes/Gateways) → Application (Controllers/Handlers) → Domain (Services/Logic) → Infrastructure (Repositories/Adapters).
- Use API specifications (OpenAPI, GraphQL schema) as the single source of truth.
- Generate or validate scaffolds against API contracts.
- Group modules by domain feature.
- Minimize dependencies between features to isolate changes.

## Dependency Inversion & Infrastructure
- Prioritize Node.js built-in modules (fs, path, crypto) over external dependencies.
- Inject external clients (DB, Cache, APIs) into services via constructors or factories.
- Services must depend on interfaces or abstractions, not concrete implementations.
- Inject all configuration values.
- Modules must not read `process.env` directly.
- Use a centralized configuration provider that validates environment variables at startup.

## Async Patterns & Performance
- Never block the event loop with synchronous I/O or heavy CPU tasks.
- Offload intensive operations to Worker Threads or background queues.
- Use `async/await` exclusively.
- Do not mix Promise chains and callbacks.
- Set explicit timeouts for all outbound network calls.
- Implement circuit breakers for all outbound network calls.
- Use profiling tools to analyze memory leaks and event loop delays during development.

## Error Handling & Observability
- Use a hierarchy of typed errors (DomainError, InfrastructureError, ValidationError).
- Use a framework-agnostic global error handler to translate errors into structured responses.
- Catch `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` at the process level.
- Log error context and exit the process gracefully on unhandled exceptions.
- Inject a unique correlation ID at the request entry point.
- Propagate correlation IDs through all logs and downstream calls.

## Security & Boundary Defense
- Scan dependencies regularly for vulnerabilities and license compliance.
- Sanitize and validate all external input at the system boundary.
- Treat all data from the transport layer as untrusted.
- Run the process with the minimum necessary permissions.
- Use secret rotation for all credentials.
- Never hardcode credentials.
- Use parameterized queries or type-safe ORMs/Query Builders.
- String concatenation for database queries is forbidden.

## Engineering Standards
- Use Conventional Commits to automate versioning and changelogs.
- Maintain `SKILL.md` or modular instructions for complex workflows.
- Keep documentation close to the implementation.
- Maintain high unit test coverage for domain logic.
- Use integration tests for infrastructure boundaries.
